recommended.title: The Quran's First Prayer Is Answered by Its First Sentence
recommended.why: The one piece where every persona scores 4+; the universal entry point the slate needs; teaches the munasaba lens the other reveals depend on; mechanically-checkable root echo (هدي on both sides of the surah 1/2 seam) with attributed munasaba tradition.
recommended.corrections_to_apply: 1) DE-PIN THE CLASSICAL ATTRIBUTIONS (non-negotiable): before any 'classical/unimpeachably classical' claim, verify in primary Arabic that al-Razi's Mafatih al-Ghayb intro to al-Baqarah opens on the ihdina->hudan sequence and that Ibn al-Qayyim (Madarij al-Salikin) states 2:2 is God's answer to ihdina. If either cannot be pinned to a specific passage, DROP the pinned citation and reframe to: 'a celebrated munasaba (tanasub al-suwar), rooted in the classical framing of al-Fatiha as du'a (Ibn al-Qayyim) and stated crisply by later mufassirun including Mawdudi (Tafhim al-Qur'an)' — the crispest attested wording of this exact reading is modern, so do not sell it as unimpeachably classical on unverifiable citations. 2) Say 'same root (هدي)', NOT 'word-for-word' — 1:6 is an imperative verb (ihdina), 2:2 a noun (hudan). 3) Keep the basmala-numbering caution (Hafs counts basmala as 1:1): say 'closing request / first content-sentence', never 'last ayah / verse 1'. 4) Phrase ihdina as the closing REQUEST, the du'a unit 1:6-7. 5) Do NOT inflate the attested seam-reading into an unattributed global 'the whole Quran is compositionally structured as an answered du'a'; keep it 'the seam reads as request-and-answer.' 6) Build on / quiet-hand link the existing content/tadabbur/001-al-fatiha/ayahs-006-007 tadabbur (which already frames 1:6 as 'the first du'a') rather than re-presenting it as new; since the site already uses the seam-munasaba lens (Isra->Kahf in the Kahf 001-005 page), scope 'rare structural reveal' to the CONTENT, not the method. 7) Keep the payoff on the 2:2 TEXTUAL answer; do not let the hadith qudsi ('I divided the prayer...') that Ibn Kathir cites on 1:6-7 become the proof, or the piece flips to a hadith payoff. 8) Keep it short — resist over-writing a 90-second reveal; let quiet-hand links carry the depth.

recommended.title: The Storm Changes the Grammar: Why God Stops Calling the Sailors 'You'
recommended.why: Best warrant-to-payoff in the pool — verbatim classical tafsir (al-Jalalayn 'fihi iltifat 'an al-khitab' on wa-jarayna bihim) on a verse everyone can feel; person-marking is mechanically verifiable; inaugurates iltifat as a named category future pronoun articles build on. Khalil/Yusuf get a named classical category with verbatim citation; Amina/Sara feel the diagnosis without Arabic.
recommended.corrections_to_apply: 1) Name the category and direction precisely: iltifat min al-khitab ila al-ghaybah (address -> absence) at wa-jarayna bihim, attributed to classical tafsir (al-Jalalayn verbatim). 2) Reframe the cross-passage layer: do NOT say the choreography 'repeats'. State that 6:63-64, 17:67, 31:32 form a FAMILY handling the God-address differently — 17:67 stays entirely 2nd person, 31:32 stays entirely 3rd, 6:63's vow says 'He' (anjana, 3MS) — and that ONLY 10:22 completes the full you->them->You-to-God turn. Keep the four-verse map bracketed as modern synthesis / flagged-modern coda. 3) Verify al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) / al-Razi against primary text before asserting, or DROP the 'paradigm/textbook case' superlative and rest the classical grounding on the confirmed al-Jalalayn verbatim alone. 4) Attribute only the DEVICE to classical tafsir; present the comfort->forgetting->distance reading explicitly as tadabbur/reflection, not the mufassir's stated reason (al-Zamakhshari's classical rationale for the turn is i'rad — recounting the sailors' ingratitude to others — layer the modern distance-of-the-heart reading ON TOP of that, do not replace it). 5) Keep the narration honest: the storyline stays 3rd person through the ENTIRE storm (ja'ahum / zannu / da'aw all 3MP); narration never resumes addressing the passengers as 'you'. The only 2nd person that returns is the sailors' QUOTED speech to God (anjaytana). 6) Distinguish the two second persons — the theological point: opening 'you' (2MP) is God->mankind; storm 'You' (2MS) is mankind->God — the direction REVERSES. 7) Cross-link (don't restate) the existing content/tadabbur/010-yunus/ayahs-021-024 tadabbur, which covers the psychological rhythm (crisis sincerity, storms strip to tawhid) but not the pronoun choreography — foreground the pronoun mechanism as the article's reason to exist. 8) No phonetic-symbolism drift; keep claims where the person-marking evidence is.

recommended.title: Everyone Blames Eve. The Verse That Assigns the Fault Uses the Singular — and Names Adam.
recommended.why: The Amina/Sara acquisition piece — 'does Islam blame Eve' is a perennial contested-verse query (the site's proven acquisition channel) with no rigorous English answer built on verifiable morphology plus named tafsir. HASAN-4 over YASMIN-1 because the 20:122 election-and-tawbah counterweight is built in, so it cannot be flipped into 'the Quran blames Adam instead.' Sara reads it with her 14-year-old; the WhatsApp forward.
recommended.corrections_to_apply: 1) Rewrite the overlap note to disclose and differentiate from BOTH content/tadabbur/020-ta-ha/ayahs-121-122 (already notes the dual->singular verb-subject shift) and content/tadabbur/007-al-araf/ayahs-023-025 (already frames 7:23 as the opposite of Iblis); cite them as the site's own groundwork the article synthesizes — do NOT present the pronoun-shift or the confession-vs-Iblis contrast as fresh discoveries. 2) Narrow the genuinely-new legs to: the 'does Islam blame Eve' reader-wound framing, that Eve is never named in the Quran (verified: zero Hawwa tokens in corpus), and the Genesis divergence. 3) Keep the 'if anything, lands on Adam' HEDGE — do NOT overstate into 'the Quran blames Adam instead'; 20:122 immediately records Adam's election (ijtaba) and tawbah, so the point is shared confession, not transferred blame. State explicitly that al-Tabari / al-Muyassar gloss 20:121's disobedience as dual/shared, so the classical tradition did NOT read the singular as exculpating Eve — the singular-isolates-Adam inference is the article's own modern comparative reflection, clearly labeled. 4) State that 20:121 is the SOLE verse individuating the disobedience (7:22-23 keeps the reproach dual and the confession joint; 2:36 assigns the slip to Shaytan); frame as 'the one place blame is individuated, it is Adam — never Eve,' not a distributed pattern. 5) Foreground the in-verse dual->singular contrast (shared acts dual, disobedience singular) to pre-empt the 'it's just default masculine narration' rebuttal. 6) GENESIS GUARDRAIL (fold YASMIN-1's comparative-dignity discipline): Genesis 3 does NOT blame Eve alone (Adam deflects, God addresses both) — the Eve-centric blame is reception history (1 Timothy 2:14, Sirach 25:24, Augustine), not the Hebrew text; say 'the interpretive tradition around Genesis,' grant the Christian interlocutor dignity, brief paraphrase with no long quotation, descriptive never triumphal — make the claim locally: this is what THIS text does. 7) Fix 'no serpent scapegoated' — the Quran DOES name Shaytan as the tempter (2:36 azallahuma; 20:120 waswasa ilayhi); the point is that the couple do not deflect onto him, not that the text hides him. 8) Scope to the Quranic text: 'the Quran names Adam' — note that extra-Quranic tafsir / Israiliyyat (e.g. al-Tabari's al-Suddi isnad) does narrate Hawwa's role, so do not claim the tradition is silent on her.
